process_note: Each of 13 teams' cases (the original top-10 power-score shortlist, plus TB/LAC/LA added mid-run — see below) was built by an Advocate (live research), stress-tested by an independent Skeptic subagent (fresh context, own WebSearch, looking only for flaws), and resolved by an independent Arbiter subagent (fresh context, saw only positives/negatives) that weighed both sides. Calibration lessons were threaded into all three stages: trap flags reserved for teams with a concrete, checkable signal rather than narrative alone; SF's huge raw favorite status got real scrutiny per the vegas_favorite_bias lesson. SHORTLIST-METHODOLOGY UPDATE: the original run's shortlist (top-10 by season-long power score) missed TB (~0.82 raw implied vs. a depleted, QB-controversy CLE) and LAC (~0.75 raw implied vs. LV) because their own full-season point-differential blend is mediocre (TB prior -1.82/current -6.0; LAC prior +0.83/current -12.0) even though this week's specific opponent is much weaker — the power-score ranking measures team quality, not the matchup-specific gap, so correctly blending prior-season data doesn't fix this. Separately, LA (Rams) was missed because one bad Week 1 game (-20.0 pd/g) dragged down an otherwise-elite prior-season blend (+8.7 pd/g) — a possible sign the current-season weight is too aggressive this early. Both are distinct, real gaps worth a calibration lesson. Given the user flagged this, TB/LAC/LA were retroactively run through the full debate: TB held up strongly (0.82 raw -> 0.76 Arbiter, only a mild discount) and now has the HIGHEST Arbiter probability on the entire board among non-excluded teams, surpassing KC's original 0.71 — the recommendation changed from KC to TB as a direct result. LAC (0.75 raw -> 0.61) and LA (0.78 raw -> 0.58) both took the two largest raw-to-Arbiter discounts on the board (confirmed multi-starter injury clusters on each), consistent with them being real trap-caliber risks, though SEA and BAL remain the two curated trap_flags per the 1-2/week cap — LAC/LA's real weaknesses are already reflected in their now-lower Arbiter numbers instead.
